A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeRF research despite the changed title. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, moved, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MeRF, RLVR, and SFT experiments on K&K puzzles, including training curves, difficulty-specific results, ablations, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original K&K experiments and reports additional model evaluations, mathematical reasoning results, CountDown experiments, and training analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions inject a natural-language reward specification into training prompts and use GRPO. The K&K prompt and correctness/format rewards are unchanged between v1 Section 3.2 and v2 Section 2.2. The new pipeline illustration and exploration analyses do not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only K&K logic puzzles. v2 retains that coverage and adds mathematical training using a DAPO-Math-17K subset, evaluation on AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, and MATH500, and CountDown arithmetic tasks using three or four numbers (Section 3.1 and Appendix A.3).

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares SFT with and without motivation against RLVR and MeRF for Qwen2.5-3B and 7B. v2 removes both SFT comparators entirely, eliminating the comparison against supervised finetuning. The named comparators in Table 1 remain unchanged; the new math comparison uses RLVR.

E3.justification: v2 adds finetuning configurations involving Qwen2.5-7B-Base, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M, and two DeepSeek-R1-Distill models. It introduces pass@k evaluation and checkpoint comparisons, and substitutes the distilled 1.5B model for Qwen2.5-3B in the prompt-gap analysis. The epoch statement changes from two to '1 and 2' without assigning budgets to experiments; retained K&K splits and GRPO hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds entropy and checkpoint pass@k analyses investigating exploration and training efficiency (Figures 4–7). It removes v1's SFT analysis, Qwen2.5-3B failure analysis, and response-length comparisons, while evaluating the motivation-removal gap on a different small model. The adverse/suboptimal motivation ablation and appendix case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions show unexplained shaded bands in some training curves without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or statistical tests. v2 introduces no defined uncertainty-estimation procedure; its pass@k evaluations change evaluation metrics rather than training-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's K&K numerical results are unchanged. v2 adds math, CountDown, and additional model results: its new Table 2 reports average pass@1 of 36.78 for MeRF versus 33.38 for RLVR, although AIME25 pass@2 is lower at 10.0 versus 16.7. v1's SFT, Qwen2.5-3B, and response-length results disappear; these are additions and removals of evidence, not same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The GRPO background moves from v1 Section 2.2 to v2 Appendix A.3, with reorganized expectation notation and an explicit importance ratio. The clipped surrogate and reward-normalized advantage are retained. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the explicitly claimed empirical contribution from K&K to logic and mathematical reasoning benchmarks. It reframes efficiency around sparse-reward exploration, and its conclusion now claims to reveal the mechanism behind MeRF. The central reward-prompting contribution and claims about motivation consistency and adverse-motivation adaptation remain.

C2.justification: v2 introduces an explanation based on improved exploration, progressively amplified pass@k gains, and avoidance of entropy collapse. It replaces v1's concrete 3B failure and larger-model-capacity discussion with negligible prompt-gap findings on different models, and adds understanding reversed scores as an alternative explanation for adverse-motivation adaptation. The stated limitations concerning static motivation and weak generalization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset-source information and a CountDown prompt/data-format example. It also promises code and reproduction instructions upon acceptance, without establishing their present availability. The existing VeRL, Logic-RL, vLLM, and most hyperparameter disclosures are retained and moved to Appendix A.3.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Cui et al. on entropy, Lightman et al. for mathematical evaluation, and Pan et al.'s TinyZero. It removes citations to Chu et al., Yue et al., and Kojima et al. The related-work discussion in Appendix A.2 and the core positioning around combining in-context learning with reinforcement finetuning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and motivation discussion around sparse-reward learning. It moves the preliminary material into the appendix, reorganizes the analysis questions around mechanisms, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v2 rebuilds Figure 1 as four accuracy panels, combining retained 7B and appendix 14B curves with new configurations while removing response-length panels. It adds a pipeline diagram, math table, entropy plots, and pass@k displays; removes the SFT table; and redraws the motivation illustration. Boxed questions, takeaways, and wrapped figures substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The new math and CountDown evaluations and exploration diagnostics strengthen evidence beyond v1's single benchmark. However, v2 removes all SFT comparisons and the documented Qwen2.5-3B failure—MeRF averaged 0.19 versus RLVR's 0.26 in v1 Table 2—while advancing broader generality and mechanism claims. Although the general weak-generalization caveat remains, the loss of concrete counterevidence materially weakens the account of applicability. These substantial benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
